transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I'm here because my eating just went completely off the rails. I usually have this whole system, but I just stopped caring about my food tracking. I'm a project manager, so I usually track everything—macros, calories, you name it. It's just like building a Gantt chart for work. Actually, I was managing this massive software migration project recently, and the vendor kept missing their milestones. It's incredibly frustrating when people don't respect the timeline, you know? I had to loop in the VP just to get them to answer my emails, and even then they tried to blame my team for the bottleneck. 

But anyway, yeah, because of everything, I was skipping real meals for days. I was basically just living on coffee and protein bars. The peanut butter ones, not the chocolate, because the chocolate always melts in my briefcase. And then my clothes started hanging really loose before I even noticed it. I actually had to punch a new hole in my belt just to keep my pants up. It's a really nice leather belt, too, my brother got it for me when I got my bachelor's degree... so I was pretty annoyed I had to ruin it with a pocket knife.
Have you noticed that you're not getting as much enjoyment or satisfaction from things you usually like doing, like hobbies or activities?

Yeah, actually, that's been happening a lot lately. I haven't wanted to hike, edit photos, log my meals, or even touch this woodworking project I have set up in my garage. It's really strange because those things usually keep me so grounded, especially the woodworking. I was building this incredible mid-century modern credenza for my living room out of walnut. Walnut is such a beautiful wood, but it's incredibly unforgiving if your tools aren't sharp enough. I spent like three hours just sharpening my chisels last month using this Japanese water stone set I imported. You have to soak the stones for exactly twenty minutes before you use them or you ruin the grit. My neighbor, Gary, he uses this cheap electric sharpener and it just destroys the temper of the steel. He asked to borrow my router once and I had to make up an excuse because I know he'd just leave it out in his damp shed and let the collet rust. But yeah, the credenza is just sitting there half-finished right now, covered in sawdust. I don't even care to look at it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has your mood been affecting your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Well, it's been going on for about three months now. Ever since that whole software migration project blew up in my face, I've just felt completely hollow. Like this heavy, shameful feeling that I just can't shake. I can't focus at work, I'm just staring at my screen. I usually have three monitors set up at my desk because it's impossible to track cross-functional dependencies on just one screen, you know? My company uses this really clunky legacy system for expense reporting, and they refuse to upgrade it. The UI is just terrible, it looks like it was built in 1995. I actually submitted a 12-page proposal to the IT director about migrating to a cloud-based platform, outlining all the ROI and efficiency gains, but he just brushed me off. He's one of those guys who thinks if it isn't completely broken, why fix it? But it *is* broken, it takes me an hour just to reconcile my travel expenses. I travel a lot for work—or I used to, anyway—mostly to Chicago. The deep dish pizza there is so overrated, honestly. It's just a casserole. If I want real pizza, I make it myself. I have this pizza stone that gets up to 800 degrees... but yeah, anyway, for the last three months, I just haven't been able to function at all. It's just this constant, empty feeling.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels or do you feel more tired than usual, even if you're not doing much?

Yeah, I mean, I guess I'm just constantly exhausted. Like, even if I've just been sitting on the couch all day, I feel like I ran a marathon. It's this deep, heavy kind of tired, you know? Like my bones are made of lead. Which is funny, because I actually used to read a lot about metallurgy when I was trying to figure out the best alloy for this custom espresso tamper I wanted to machine. I got really into espresso for a while. You can't just use any beans, obviously, you need a proper burr grinder. Blade grinders just chop the beans unevenly and you get this terrible, bitter extraction. I spent like six hundred dollars on this Italian grinder, and it was totally worth it, but the hopper is made of this really cheap acrylic that cracked the first week I had it. I tried to fix it with some two-part epoxy, but the resin didn't cure right because the humidity in my kitchen was too high. You really have to control the ambient temperature when you're working with adhesives like that. I actually have a whole spreadsheet tracking the optimal curing times based on relative humidity... but yeah, I just don't have the energy for any of that right now. I'm just so drained all the time.
Have you had any thoughts about death, or wished you were dead, or thought about harming yourself?

Yeah... yeah, I have. It got really bad a few weeks ago. I just started thinking that everyone at work would be better off if I just didn't wake up in the morning. Like, I'm just a burden, dragging the whole team down. We had this one status meeting, and I just couldn't answer a simple question about the timeline, and right after that meeting, I actually said out loud to myself that I should just walk into traffic and be done with it. Traffic around here is terrible, by the way. They've been doing construction on the I-95 corridor for, what, three years now? It's supposed to alleviate the bottleneck near the downtown exit, but all they've done is shift the congestion two miles north. I actually read the civil engineering proposal for the highway expansion because I was curious about their timeline projections. They're using this outdated predictive model for traffic flow that doesn't account for the new residential zoning laws that passed last year. It's completely flawed. If you look at the raw data, the peak volume hours have already shifted, but they're still paving the shoulder like it's 2015. I almost wrote a letter to the city planner about it, but... well, what's the point? Like I said, I just felt like I should walk into the street and let a truck hit me.
